newsitem.title: USA: CME cattle end up on short covering in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: CME cattle end up on short covering in thin trade.

text.p: Trading activity was light in CME live and feeder cattle futures alike, late as the market prepared for the long holiday weekend and prices ended higher on short covering, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.0250 to 0.275 cent per lb higher with August up 0.075 at 63.925 cents. Feeder cattle ended up 0.325 cent to unchanged with August up most at 80.950 cents.

Pre-holiday evening up resulted in mixed price action in live cattle early but late scattered short covering pushed prices up by the close. Expectations for lower fed cattle prices next week kept a lid on gains, traders said.
Packers are expected to bid $62 per cwt for fed cattle next week in light of falling boxed beef values and expected adequate feedlot offerings, they said.
The market also showed little direction from technicals as it held in the recent trading range, they added.

Rand Financials bought October late. RBH sold August early while Cargill Investor Services bought both months. In live cattle options, commission houses bought August 64 puts and sold 62 and 63 puts early. Commercials sold October 68 calls and December 72 calls late. Volatility was weak ahead of the holiday weekend, pit sources said.

Feeder cattle futures ran up late as early selling lacked follow through and prices ran up on mixed support and local short covering. Buy stops were hit above the early high and prices ran up to best levels late, they said.
Early profit taking gave way to continued support from the strong feeder cattle markets and lower corn futures. Cash cattle are seen holding strong into the fall, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.10 to $80.67 per cwt, the highest level since April 19, 1994.
Dean Witter sold September and October early. LIT division of First Options bought August late, pit sources said.

Boneless beef futures ended mostly higher and beef trimmings futures fully higher with deferred contracts in both pits again posting new contract highs. Refco bought August but local selling turned that month down. Rosenthal Collins bought August trimmings to offset speculative selling, traders said.
Boneless beef closed 0.20 cent per lb lower to 2.00 higher with only August off at 94.50 cents. Trimmings ended 0.10 to 0.20 higher with August up 0.10 at 44.10 cents.
